hook.en: Hold a tight spot with your hand while the patient actively moves the muscle from short to long beneath your contact.
hook.ur: Active Soft-Tissue Release mein clinician soft tissue par targeted contact maintain karta hai jab patient related joint ya muscle ko active movement se range mein le jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Active Soft-Tissue Release is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Active Soft-Tissue Release kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

text.en: In active-release-style work, you hold a precise contact on a restricted muscle, tendon or nerve interface and ask the patient to move the area from a shortened position into lengthening. The movement under the contact is the treatment.
text.ur: Clinician soft tissue par targeted contact rakhta hai aur patient related joint ya muscle ko actively range mein move karta hai.

simpler.en: Hold a tight spot with your hand while the patient actively moves the muscle from short to long beneath your contact.
simpler.ur: Active Soft-Tissue Release mein clinician soft tissue par targeted contact maintain karta hai jab patient related joint ya muscle ko active movement se range mein le jata hai.

text.en: Like pinning down a piece of tape while pulling the surface beneath it: the pin and the movement together free the stuck area.
text.ur: Jaise tape ke ek tukde ko dabaye rakh kar us ke neeche wali surface ko kheenchna: dabana aur movement mil kar atke hue hisse ko azaad karte hain.

text.en:
Three ideas carry this whole technique:
**1.** Shorten, contact, then lengthen actively.
**2.** The patient's own movement makes it active and functional.
**3.** Use light to moderate contact; the movement does the work.
text.ur: Yeh local pressure ko active tissue excursion aur movement exposure ke sath combine karta hai. Is se short-term flexibility, pain aur movement tolerance mein behtari ho sakti hai. Technique names aur branded systems mukhtalif hain; underlying clinical concept ko generic taur par sikhaya ja sakta hai.

question.ur: Pehle vocabulary — clinicians yeh lafz bohat use karte hain. **Shortened position** ka matlab kya hai?

text.en:
So when does **Active Soft-Tissue Release** make sense?
• Overuse tightness, such as hamstring or forearm muscle restriction.
• When you want to combine hands-on work with movement.
text.ur: Movement-related soft-tissue discomfort; selected muscle ya tendon stiffness.

text.en:
And just as important — when you should NOT use it, or should stop:
• Acute tear, infection, open wounds or bleeding disorders.
• Nerve symptoms that increase.
• Pain that rises sharply.
text.ur:
Acute strain, bruising ka rujhan ya neuropathy.
Khula zakhm, aisa acute tear jise protection chahiye, DVT ya infection.
Painful tissue ko aggressively squeeze karna, nerve symptoms ignore karna aur har limitation ko adhesion kehna avoid karein. Numbness, tingling ya radiating symptoms change hon to stop karke neurological status reassess karein.

title.en: How to do it — 6 steps, each with its reason
title.ur: Kaise karein — 6 qadam, har ek ki wajah ke saath

steps.title: Locate the restriction
steps.detail: Find the tight spot during movement and palpation.

steps.title: Shorten the muscle
steps.detail: Place the area in a shortened position.

steps.title: Apply contact
steps.detail: Press firmly but comfortably on the spot.

steps.title: Ask for slow active lengthening
steps.detail: The patient actively moves the muscle toward lengthening while you hold.

steps.title: Retest and load
steps.detail: Retest movement and add a strengthening exercise.

beats.ur:
1. Clinically relevant soft-tissue region identify karein.
2. Tissue par controlled contact rakhein.
3. Agar munasib ho to tissue ko shortened position mein rakhein.
4. Contact maintain karte hue patient se actively tissue lengthen ya range mein move karwayein.
5. Target movement dobara assess karein.

question.ur: Farz karein patient aap ke saamne hai. Aap SAB SE PEHLE kya karenge?

text.en: How much? Typical teaching range: 3-5 passes per spot, a few spots per session. Keep contact tolerable and stop if symptoms spread.
text.ur: Aksar har target area par 3–8 slow repetitions. Pressure bardasht ke qabil rakhein aur bruising paida karne se bachein.

beats.patient: Ben, 28, runner with tight left hamstring when extending the knee.
beats.assessment: A tender spot mid-hamstring; knee extension limited.
beats.treatment: With the knee bent, you contact the spot; he slowly straightens his knee. Repeat 4 passes.
beats.reassess: Knee extension improves and tenderness drops. Strengthening follows.
beats.ur:
Ek misal se poora clinical flow dekhein:
Farz karein elbow bend karne par forearm ke ek soft-tissue area mein tightness mehsoos hoti hai. Clinician controlled contact ke sath patient se ahista movement karwata hai aur phir range dobara check karta hai. Yeh sirf illustrative example hai.

text.en:
The mistakes I see most often:
• Rushing the active movement.
• Pressing too hard.
• Not combining with strengthening.
text.ur:
Sab se aam ghaltiyan:
• Rushing the active movement.
• Pressing too hard.
• Not combining with strengthening.

text.en: Studies are limited and low in quality, with some short-term improvements. The idea of breaking adhesions has little direct evidence.
text.ur: Treatment ke baad relevant movement, strength ya task tolerance check karein. Branded ya style-based techniques ke evidence ko universal proof na samjhein; active loading aur broader rehabilitation ki importance maintain karein.

text.en: One line to carry into the clinic: **Shorten, hold, lengthen actively, retest.**
text.ur: Active movement is concept ki key feature hai; pressure tissue ko guide kare, overpower nahi.
